svg.title: PlaSiC radiation parameterization: from model state to layer heating rates
svg.desc: Common inputs and the layer-mass conversion feed the shortwave and longwave branches. The shortwave branch converts cloud water into an optical depth, evaluates two-stream cloud optics for both spectral bands and both illumination directions, inserts Rayleigh scattering only at the lowest layer, combines gas absorption and cloud scattering into layer reflectance and transmittance with the surface albedo as the lower boundary, and finally runs the adding recursion. The longwave branch computes Planck fluxes, gas broadband transmittances, cloud emissivity with random overlap, directional effective emission, and vertical integration. The branches merge into the net downward flux, and its divergence gives the radiative temperature tendency.
svg.text: One Radiation Calculation: From Model State to Layer Heating Rates
Common inputs → shortwave reflection–transmission and longwave absorption–emission in parallel → net flux divergence

g.text: COMMON INPUTS
Solar–Earth geometry
Latitude φ, declination δ, hour angle h, orbit
μ0 = cos θ0; distance correction dr
μ0 = 0 on the night side → no shortwave
Atmospheric profiles
ps, σ layers, T, q, O3, CO2
Layer-center state and interface positions
Local mixing ratios are not used directly by the fits
Cloud and surface state
Cloud cover Cl, cloud water qc, surface type
Surface Ts, albedo α, emissivity εs
Clouds affect both shortwave and longwave
First convert local mixing ratios into layer column amounts
Δml = psΔσl / g | ΔuX,l = qX,lΔml
Then apply direction, pressure, and temperature corrections to obtain effective path amounts

svg.text: LONGWAVE (LW): surface and atmosphere both emit

g.text: Project solar energy into two spectral bands
F0,b = wb S0 dr μ0
0.517: visible/UV (O3, Rayleigh & cloud scattering)
0.483: near-IR (H2O, cloud scattering + absorption)
Temperature into a thermal emission scale
B(T) = σSBT4
Interpolate B to layer interfaces
Accumulate H2O, O3, CO2 effective amounts between levels
Gas paths → single-layer transmittance
Band 1 (O3): direct M(μ0), diffuse Md = 1.9
Band 2 (H2O): M(μ0) direct, Md = 1.66; p and T corrections
Tg,l = P(Xl) / P(Xl−1)
Clear-sky broadband transmittance
Evaluate H2O, O3, CO2 broadband absorption
Correct H2O–CO2 band overlap to avoid double counting
Tclear(i,j) = clip[1 − AH2O − AO3 − ACO2,corr]
Cloud optics and Rayleigh scattering
Band 1 — scattering only
Band 2 — scattering and absorption
β1 = fb1 √μ
β2 = fb2 √μ / ln(3 + 0.1 τN)
Rc1 = β1τN / (μ + β1τN)
Tc1 = 1 − Rc1
Tc2 = 4u/D, Rc2 = 2(u2 − 1) sinh(τeff)/D
Rayleigh (band 1, lowest layer): Rdir = 0.219/(1 + 0.816 μ0), Rdif = 0.144
Cloud emissivity and random overlap
εc,l = 1 − exp(−1.66 kcWL,l)
Tcloud(i,j) = ∏l∈(i,j) [1 − Clεc,l]
Only radiation crossing every transparent fraction continues
Layer optics and the surface boundary
Band 1: Rl,1 = zrcsl + ClRc,l,1, Tl,1 = 1 − (1 − Tg,l,1)(1 − Cl) − Rl,1
Band 2: Rl,2 = ClRc,l,2, Tl,2 = 1 − (1 − Tg,l,2)(1 − Cl) − (1 − Tc,l,2)Cl
Starred (upward) properties: same relations with upward gas transmittance and cloud optics
Single-layer closure: Al,b = 1 − Rl,b − Tl,b, so R + T + A = 1
Lower boundary: Rs = αs, the area-weighted land / sea-ice / open-ocean albedo
Ice-free ocean direct albedo = min[0.05/(μ0 + 0.15), 0.15]
Total transmittance between interfaces
T(i,j) = Tclear(i,j) · Tcloud(i,j)
Keeps band saturation; not a plain product of layer transmittances
1 − T is the absorptance and emissivity of the path (Kirchhoff's law)
Bidirectional adding over the whole column
Merge downward from the top of the atmosphere; upward from the surface
1 / (1 − R*upper Rlower)
Analytically sums unlimited round trips between the two subsystems
Directional emission of non-isothermal layers
Linear B in pressure; exponential transmittance across the layer
Bu: upward emission at layer top | Bd: downward at base
Optically weighted effective fluxes, not two real layer temperatures
Interface shortwave fluxes
DSWl, USWl: sum the two bands weighted by F0,b
One up/down flux pair per interface for each band
Interface longwave fluxes
Sum layer emissions that reach the interface
Weight = difference of cumulative transmittances
DLWTOA = 0; ULWs = εsBs + (1 − εs) DLWs
Form the SW and LW net downward fluxes, then merge
FSWl = DSWl − USWl, FLWl = DLWl − ULWl, Fl = FSWl + FLWl
Convention: D and U are positive magnitudes; F is positive downward
Adjacent-interface flux difference → layer heating → radiative tendency
(∂T/∂t)rad,l = −g (Fl+1 − Fl) / [cppsΔσl(1 + avql)]
Fl+1 < Fl: heating | Fl+1 > Fl: net radiative loss, cooling

svg.text: Outputs: up/down fluxes at every interface, TOA and surface budgets, and per-layer SW / LW / total radiative tendencies
